newsitem.title: USA: Nixon estate may be paid for papers - report.
newsitem.headline: Nixon estate may be paid for papers - report.

text.p: The U.S. government would pay the estate of former President Richard Nixon $26 million for his White House papers and records under a proposed settlement, the Washington Post reported on Saturday.

The newspaper said under the still-tentative agreement, details of which had been confirmed by both government sources and those close to the Nixon family, the estate has agreed to turn over to the National Archives control of the privately run Nixon library in Yorba Linda, Calif.
All the materials seized by the government as Nixon attempted to spirit them from the White House following his resignation in 1974 would be shipped to California as well, the Post said.
The Richard Nixon Library and Birthplace Foundation would use part of the payment, reportedly about $8 million, to build a new facility to house the collection of more than 44 million items.
The Post said the agreement left unchanged the complex network of rules and timetables governing and restricting the public's access to the materials.
The proposed settlement would bring the Nixon library, which opened in 1990 with the unique distinction of having no original presidential documents, in line with other presidential libraries.
Nixon's papers and records are now held in the National Archives annex in College Park, Md.
The Post said no modern-day president had been directly paid for his papers, although some had taken sizable tax deductions for their donations.
